title: sales partnership scratch notes - acme fintech POC
content:
ACME Financial (target) — quick notes and outbound drafts

Context / why I'm chasing:
- Large US-based fintech (payments + lending) evaluating embedding LLM features into merchant dashboard and merchant support tooling.
- Early exec signal: Head of ML (John Doe) wants faster inference and lower cost for high-throughput chat+assistant workflows — current infra: combo of managed LLM endpoints + internal CPU-based rerank.
- Trigger: new merchant growth initiative (Nov 2025 roadmap) — want automated merchant onboarding + 24/7 assistant for high volume.

Key contacts (intel):
- John Doe — Head of ML (linkedin: https://linkedin.com/in/john-doe-1223). Likely technical champion.
- Priya Singh — Dir Product, Merchant Experience. Budget owner for pilot.
- Marcus Lee — Infra Eng lead (SRE). Concerned about data isolation / VPC.

Tech stack / current pain points:
- Current models: mix of 3rd-party hosted APIs (expensive per-token) + small in-house models on CPU for specific reranking tasks.
- Pain: unpredictable latency spikes during morning peak (merchant timezone overlap), cost blowouts on high-volume batching, lack of per-route observability.
- Compliance: PCI-adjacent data, want Private deployment or at least VPC peering + KMS.

POC / win criteria (what they care about):
- 95th percentile latency under 350ms for short assistant prompts (<= 512 tokens) during peak load.
- 3x reduction in per-conversation inference cost vs current hosted provider for same quality baseline.
- Integration time <= 8 weeks with sample dataset + limited production traffic.
- Controls: encryption at rest, KMS integration, audit logs.

Suggested POC scope (short):
- Phase 0: baseline measurement (1 week) — run shadow traffic through Redwood hosted API to capture latencies/costs (no customer-facing changes).
- Phase 1: dedicated capacity pilot (4 weeks) — spin up Dedicated instance, integrate one assistant route, measure latency/cost under synthetic peak.
- Phase 2: private deployment (optional, 4-6 weeks) — if compliance requires, deploy Private with VPC peering + KMS.

Pricing / commercial signals:
- They currently spend ~$80k/mo on hosted provider across multiple teams (estimate). Pilots budget: $25k-$40k Q1.
- Likely ask: monthly committed capacity or consumption with committed minimum.

Potential objections and quick rebuttals:
- "We already have an endpoint provider — switching is risky": highlight feature parity + migration path: run shadow, fallback policy, identical API handlers. Emphasize iteration speed and cost savings measured during pilot.
- "Data security / PCI": Redwood Private + KMS + audit logs. Offer architecture diagram and SRE workshop; propose temporary NDA + SOC docs.
- "We need predictable capacity": propose Dedicated with reserved pools + autoscaling and SLA. Show perf profiles from similar customers (payments vertical).
- "Quality/regression concerns": propose eval harness and prompt set regression alerts; include sample evals comparing model variants.

Outbound email drafts (short / informal)
- Subject options (iterate): "Quick idea for ACME's merchant support latency/cost", "Reduce inference cost for ACME merchant assistant", "Redwood x ACME — pilot proposal (short)"

Email draft 1 (cold warm intro):
Hi John —
I saw the merchant growth work you're shipping and had a quick idea that could reduce inference cost and latency for your merchant assistant without a full infra rewrite. We ran a similar Dedicated pilot with a payments company and cut per-convo costs ~3x while improving peak P95 latency.
Would you be open to a 20-min call next week to see if a short shadow test makes sense? Happy to share a one-page POC plan.
— Danielle

Phone / call script (30 min):
- 0-5: quick intros + confirm pain (latency, cost, compliance).
- 5-10: confirm traffic shape (QPS, token distribution, peak windows).
- 10-18: propose POC (shadow -> dedicated pilot -> private optional). Show similar case study numbers.
- 18-25: technical questions from Marcus — be ready to talk about VPC, KMS, KV caching, batching, fallback.
- 25-30: next steps: shadow test + data ingest checklist.

Qualification questions to ask early:
- What is current peak QPS and 95th percentile latency for assistant routes?
- Average tokens per conversation and typical prompt length?
- Who owns procurement for pilots (SaaS contract)?
- Any hard regulatory requirements (PCI, SOC, GDPR for EU merchants)?

Notes / internal TODOs:
- Slack intro: #sales-partnerships -> @Jordan Kim with brief summary and ask for perf profile from payments case study.
- Prepare 1-pager + architecture diagram (include Dedicated + Private options).
- Ask solutions-eng to draft temporary SRE runbook for VPC peering steps.
- Collect 2 example prompts and token counts from Priya during discovery call.

Possible red flags:
- Procurement cycle >6 months (enterprise legal/ops slow). If so, move to quick shadow as low-friction path.
- Heavy encryption + HSM-only requirement (might delay Private). Flag to infra early.

Quick links / references to include in outreach:
- Redwood one-pager (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SALES/Redwood-One-Pager
- Payments case study (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SALES/Payments-Case-Study

Next actions (this week):
- Send intro email to John (A/B subject lines).
- Ping solutions-eng for a 30-min readiness check (can we spin Dedicated pilot in 2-4 weeks?).
- Draft shadow test script + minimal sample dataset request (send to Priya on discovery).

-- end of notes --

(Notes to self: keep emails short, include quant metrics up-front, offer shadow test as low friction. If Marcus asks about fallback: mention automatic routing to a cheaper variant and canary rollouts in Redwood Console.)
